note: Informational starting point: no guideline restricts potassium or phosphorus at G1-G2 unless serum levels run high (KDOQI 2020 6.3.1/6.4.1; K/DOQI 2004 lists > 4,000 mg/day potassium for G1-G2). Protein: the general-population RDA of 0.8 g/kg is the floor and KDIGO 2024 PP 3.3.1.1 says to avoid > 1.3 g/kg; 1.0 is a conservative ceiling. Sodium < 2,000 mg (KDIGO 2024 Rec 3.3.2.1). Fluid: no routine limit. Calories: KDOQI 2020 3.1.1 range 25-35 kcal/kg; per kg of a reference weight (KDOQI leaves the choice of weight to the care team, 1.1.6). Calcium: KDOQI 2020 6.2.1 800-1,000 mg total incl. supplements/binders. The care team overwrites every value.

Same as stage 1: informational potassium/phosphorus ceilings (restriction only if serum potassium or phosphate is high), protein 0.8 g/kg RDA floor with a 1.0 ceiling (KDIGO: avoid > 1.3), sodium < 2,000 mg, no routine fluid limit, 30 kcal/kg (KDOQI 25-35), calcium 1,000 mg total.

Potassium 4,000 mg is a review ceiling, not a prescription: guidelines give no mg number (KDOQI 2020 6.4.1 adjust to keep serum K normal; KDIGO 2024 PP 3.11.5.2 limit bioavailable potassium if hyperkalaemic); K/DOQI 2004 range for G3a-G4 is 2,000-4,000 mg/day. If serum K > 5.0-5.5 mmol/L use 2,000-3,000 mg (AKF: aim 2,500, no more than 3,000). Phosphorus 1,000 mg = top of the KDOQI 2003 800-1,000 mg range used when serum phosphate > 4.6 mg/dL; phosphate additives are flagged regardless of total. Protein 0.8 g/kg reference body weight with diabetes (ADA 2026 Rec 11.3, A: below 0.8 'is not recommended'; KDIGO 2022 Rec 3.1.1 and KDIGO 2024 Rec 3.3.1.1, 2C); KDOQI 2020 3.0.2's 0.6-0.8 (OPINION) is only for close clinical supervision, so the app never suggests it (note 05 fact-check H1). Without diabetes 0.6-0.8 g/kg (KDOQI 2020 3.0.1, 1A, under close supervision; KDIGO 2024 Rec 3.3.1.1: 0.8). Sodium < 2,000 mg (KDIGO 2024 3.3.2.1, 2C). No routine fluid limit. 30 kcal/kg (KDOQI 25-35). Calcium 800-1,000 mg total for CKD 3-4 not on active vitamin D (KDOQI 2020 6.2.1).

As 3a, with the potassium review ceiling tightened to 3,500 mg because hyperkalaemia becomes more likely as GFR falls (KDIGO 2024: prevalence 8.8 % at G3/A1 rising to 34.4 % at G5/A3 in people with diabetes); still inside the K/DOQI 2004 2,000-4,000 mg range for G3a-G4. Replace with 2,000-3,000 mg once a restriction is actually prescribed. Protein as 3a: 0.8 g/kg with diabetes (ADA 2026 Rec 11.3), 0.6-0.8 g/kg without (KDOQI 2020 3.0.1).

Potassium 3,000 mg matches Kalantar-Zadeh & Fouque (NEJM 2017) < 3 g/day for CKD 4-5 and the top of the AKF 2,500-3,000 mg patient goal; when hyperkalaemic, use 2,000-3,000 mg. Phosphorus 1,000 mg (KDOQI 2003 800-1,000 when serum phosphate > 4.6 mg/dL at stages 3-4). Protein 0.8 g/kg with diabetes (ADA 2026 Rec 11.3; KDIGO 2022 Rec 3.1.1), 0.6-0.8 g/kg without (KDOQI 2020 3.0.1). Fluid: no routine limit, but AKF notes stages 3-5 may be restricted individually if there is oedema. Calcium 800-1,000 mg total (KDOQI 2020 6.2.1).

Potassium 2,500 mg = the AKF daily goal when a restriction is prescribed (aim 2,500, no more than 3,000) and within NEJM 2017 < 3 g/day for CKD 4-5. Phosphorus 900 mg sits mid-range of KDOQI 2003 800-1,000 mg (restriction indicated when serum phosphate > 5.5 mg/dL at stage 5, EVIDENCE); binders are added when diet is not enough. Protein 0.8 g/kg with diabetes (ADA 2026 Rec 11.3; KDIGO 2022 Rec 3.1.1), 0.6-0.8 g/kg without (KDOQI 2020 3.0.1), until dialysis starts. Fluid: individualised (oedema, hyponatraemia), null here. Calcium: adjust to avoid hypercalcaemia (KDOQI 2020 6.2.2); 1,000 mg total as the starting point.

Fluid: the hemodialysis convention is 1,000 mL (32 oz) per day PLUS the person's measured 24-hour urine volume (DaVita, AKF); 1,500 mL is the default here and assumes about 500 mL of urine — replace it with the dialysis unit's personal allowance and re-measure urine every ~3 months. Potassium 2,500 mg (expert opinion 2,700-3,000 mg for HD; AKF aim 2,500, no more than 3,000; dietitian practice 2,000-3,000). Phosphorus 1,000 mg 'adjusted for protein needs' (KDOQI 2003), binders with meals. Protein 1.0-1.2 g/kg reference body weight (KDOQI 2020 3.0.3, 1C on HD; 3.0.4 with diabetes, OPINION; KDIGO 2022 PP 3.1.2; ADA 2026 Rec 11.3, B). Sodium < 2,000-2,300 mg (NKF HD diet < 2,300). Calcium: adjust to avoid hypercalcaemia counting calcium-based binders (KDOQI 2020 6.2.2; KDIGO 2017 4.1.6). Potassium, sodium and fluid also accumulate between sessions, so the app totals them over the interdialytic interval.

Peritoneal dialysis is continuous, so potassium is usually liberalised: 3,500 mg sits inside the 3,000-4,000 mg 'liberal' PD diet (DaVita; expert opinion 3.0-4.0 g/day). Fluid 2,000 mL is inside the typical 2-3 L/day and must be individualised to residual kidney function and ultrafiltration. Protein 1.0-1.2 g/kg, often the upper end ('particularly peritoneal dialysis', KDIGO 2022 PP 3.1.2; KDOQI 2020 3.0.3, OPINION on PD; 3.0.4 with diabetes). Phosphorus 1,000 mg adjusted for protein needs, binders with meals. Sodium 2,000 mg by guideline although PD programs often allow 3,000-4,000 mg. Calories: subtract the dextrose absorbed from dialysate (often 400+ kcal/day) from the 30 kcal/kg food allowance and count it as carbohydrate for insulin. Calcium: adjust to avoid hypercalcaemia (KDOQI 2020 6.2.2).
